Job Description
Contacts prospective customers in order to provide consultative advice on current cash flow practices in order to develop treasury management business. Manages relationships with existing customers to ensure proper servicing of accounts and to expand existing business. Prepares sales presentations, explains services offered, and recommends solutions which would benefit clients. Identifies opportunities to sell other U.S. Bancorp products and services to meet customer needs. Assists management in developing a market strategy and in setting sales objectives. Responsible for meeting or exceeding all assigned sales and revenue retention goals. Assists in the design and oversees the proper installation of treasury management services. Assists management in the development of new services or the modification of existing services.

Basic Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree, or equivalent work experience
- 10 or more years of related experience

Preferred Skills/Experience
- Extensive knowledge of treasury management products
- Thorough knowledge of the organization and its products, services and operations
- Strong sales and new business development skills
- Excellent customer service/relations skills
- Excellent presentation, verbal and written communication skills

jobs.title: TPS Strategy and Transformation Leader
jobs.description:
At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions and enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed.  We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive at every stage of your career. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.

Job Description
The TPS Strategy and Transformation Leader is responsible for spearheading the TPS strategy agenda. The leader will translate insights from external trends, competitive intelligence, and internal performance into long-range strategic choices and value pathways. Reporting directly to the TPS executive leader, this individual will serve as a strategic thought partner responsible for shaping growth priorities, transformation initiatives, investment decisions, and strategic execution across TPS. This individual acts as the primary partner in developing strategy, scenario planning, capital allocation, and enterprise prioritization, with transformation serving as the mechanism for executing strategic choices.

Key Responsibilities:
TPS Strategy Development and Cross-PMI Project Leadership
- Own and lead a portfolio of business-wide strategic projects requiring cross-PMI collaboration.
- Drive high-growth initiatives focused on increasing fee revenue and market share.
- Develop trusted partnerships with senior leaders and collaborate with internal and external stakeholders.
- Partner with Business Insights to conduct market and sector scans, industry trend analysis, and external benchmarking to identify disruptive forces.
- Connect the dots across businesses to deliver optimal solutions to clients.
- Lead the development of executive-level strategy narratives, deliverables, and analyses in partnership with TPS and PMI leadership. Areas of focus will include long-term value creation, strategy reviews, capital allocation, investment priorities, risk, competitive threats, and restructuring needs.
- Develop clear, insight-driven strategy narratives for executive audience
- Translate complex strategic issues and analytical findings into concise recommendations that enable executive decision-making.

Strategic Planning and Commercial Excellence
- Lead annual and multi-year strategic planning activities, including Horizon 2 and Horizon 3 planning, to ensure alignment with enterprise and PMI priorities and capital-allocation parameters.
- Manage a portfolio of strategic bets, including divestitures, new-market entry, adjacencies, and business-model innovations.
- Identify growth opportunities across market expansion, customer segmentation, value-based pricing, new-product strategy, ecosystem partnerships, and line-of-business growth.
- Develop a repeatable product-commercialization framework that supports initiatives from incubation through launch.
- Partner with senior leaders to evaluate portfolio choices and translate long-range strategy into executable priorities.

Strategic Investments
- Collaborate with the PMI CAO organization, Enterprise Strategy, Finance, Corporate Development, and business leaders to develop M&A theses, diligence frameworks, and integration strategies.
- Assess build, buy, and partner options based on strategic fit and potential synergies, partnering with Finance.
- Represent TPS in strategic discussions involving potential M&A, partnership, and bolt-on opportunities.
- Ensure the TPS operating model supports strategic priorities through effective governance, clear decision rights, and measurable KPIs.
- Use OKRs selectively to translate strategy into measurable outcomes.

Executive Partnership and Strategic Influence
- Partner with senior leaders across TPS, PMI, Enterprise Strategy, Corporate Development, and Finance to shape growth priorities, strategic investments, and transformation initiatives.
- Influence decisions and move complex initiatives forward across organizational boundaries without relying on direct reporting authority.
- Develop and refine executive communications, strategic presentations, and recommendations for senior-leadership and governance forums.
- Coach and guide analysts and junior team members supporting strategic initiatives, whether or not they report directly to this position.

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills
- Twelve or more years of experience in corporate strategy, enterprise strategy, or management consulting, with experience supporting complex business and transformation agendas.
- Experience in financial services, banking, payments, fintech, or a closely related industry.
- Exceptional quantitative and analytical problem-solving skills.
- Demonstrated ability to develop executive-level narratives and communicate complex strategic recommendations clearly to senior leaders.
- Excellent oral and written communication skills, with the ability to work effectively in cross-functional teams.
- Strong leadership, stakeholder-management, and influencing skills, including the ability to operate effectively without direct authority.
- Strong understanding of financial concepts, operating models, capital-allocation considerations, and industry and payments trends.
- Ability to organize and prioritize critical issues to support timely and effective decision-making.
- Experience coaching and developing junior talent, including team members who may not report directly to the position, while overseeing high-priority projects.

Preferred Skills and Experience
- Undergraduate or graduate degree in Economics, Finance, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related field.
- Experience in corporate or enterprise strategy within a bank or other financial-services organization.
- Experience in a top-tier strategy-consulting environment.
- Experience applying data analysis to solve business problems in fast-paced environments.
- Cross-functional collaboration experience, including influencing stakeholders and working with diverse teams.
- Experience advising senior leaders on growth strategy, market entry, product launches, partnership evaluations, portfolio choices, and operating-model design.
- Experience applying structured problem-solving and design-thinking methods to strategic priorities.
- Ability to gather, analyze, and present data, including financial modeling and industry research, to senior executives.
- Experience developing strategic presentations and executive narratives for internal and external audiences.
- Experience monitoring industry trends and sharing relevant insights across teams.
- Experience collaborating across functions and businesses to deliver client-focused solutions.
- Experience shaping three- to five-year business strategies, defining growth opportunities, and identifying sources of competitive advantage.

Ideal Candidate Profile
- Twelve or more years of experience in corporate strategy, enterprise strategy, or top-tier management consulting.
- A background combining strategy experience with knowledge of banking, financial services, or payments is strongly preferred.
- Experience from a leading strategy-consulting firm is highly valued.
- Proven experience in strategy formulation, market insights, portfolio strategy, and growth strategy.
- Demonstrated ability to lead significant strategic initiatives and manage senior stakeholders in a complex, matrixed organization.
- Ability to combine rigorous analysis with clear executive storytelling and practical execution.

Outcomes and Goals
- Value Creation: Help deliver business revenue targets and establish TPS’s growth trajectory through 2030.
- Growth Acceleration: Achieve revenue uplift through portfolio focus, go-to-market excellence, and digital and AI strategies, while increasing productivity in priority functions.
- Operating Model Modernization: Establish a target operating model with clear accountabilities, decision rights, governance, and business rhythms, including product and sales reviews, strategic client reviews, and business reviews.
- Program Durability: Build an enduring transformation capability embedded in the operating rhythm and aligned with aspirational goals rather than benchmarks alone.

jobs.title: Global Custody Strategy Manager
jobs.description:
At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions and enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed.  We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive at every stage of your career. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.

Job Description
The Global Custody Strategy Manager will own the strategy, commercial roadmap, pricing discipline, margin management, competitive positioning, and investment priorities for U.S. Bank’s Global Custody offering. This client- and industry-facing role serves as the dedicated commercial and strategic owner for custody, creating clear accountability for revenue growth, client profitability, modernization, and scalable growth.

The role will partner closely with the Head of Custody for Asset Managers and the Product Office (CPO) on the strategy roadmap, capability development, and investment priorities, while also working across Operations, Network Management, Technology, Risk, Strategy Development, Finance, Relationship Management, and business-line leadership to define where U.S. Bank should invest, how custody capabilities should evolve, and how the strategy should be positioned across asset managers, fund sponsors, and Corporate Trust / structured finance clients.

This role will translate client needs, market trends, service issues, and financial performance into a prioritized roadmap, investment cases, pricing framework, and growth plan.

Essential Functions:

Strategy & Commercial Ownership
- Define and execute the Global Custody strategy in alignment with Global Investment Services’ strategic priorities and the emerging Custody Asset Management vertical.
- Partner with CPO on the custody strategy roadmap, including prioritization of new capabilities, service enhancements, and investment cases to improve competitiveness, client experience, scalability, and profitability.
- Establish a disciplined strategy framework covering economics, client segmentation, capability prioritization, competitive positioning, and go-to-market planning.
- Translate demand across mutual funds, ETFs, alternatives, CLOs, structured products, and asset-manager custody relationships into prioritized strategic opportunities.

Revenue, Margin & P&L Discipline
- Own the custody commercial model with Finance, including revenue growth planning, margin analysis, client profitability reporting, pricing effectiveness, and financial performance routines.
- Build revenue, margin, and client profitability dashboards to support transparent leadership decision-making.
- Evaluate custody economics, pricing models, sub-custodian costs, deposit economics, and investment prioritization across custody segments.
- Develop and maintain a pricing framework and segment strategy that supports profitable growth, commercial consistency, and competitive positioning.

Client, Market & Competitive Positioning
- Serve as the strategic subject-matter expert for Global Custody in client, prospect, consultant, and industry discussions.
- Develop competitive intelligence on peer custodians, service models, pricing approaches, investment trends, and emerging custody capabilities.
- Partner with Marketing and business leadership to develop client-facing collateral, strategic positioning, and launch materials.
- Identify cross-sell opportunities across custody-adjacent businesses, including fund services, Corporate Trust / structured finance, cash, liquidity, securities lending, and related solutions.

Strategy Roadmap, Investment Prioritization & Transformation
- Own the strategy roadmap in close partnership with the Product Office (CPO), aligning capability development and investment priorities with client needs, financial returns, operational readiness, service quality, and strategic growth objectives.
- Partner with Technology, Operations, Transformation, Network Management, Risk, and business partners to modernize custody capabilities, improve data quality, standardize workflows, and prepare for new products or regulatory change.
- Convert recurring service issues, inquiry themes, market pain points, and operational constraints into product roadmap priorities.
- Develop business cases for strategic enhancements, platform investments, market expansion, automation, and new custody capabilities.

Operating Model Partnership & Governance
- Partner with Operations, Network Management, Technology, Risk, and CAO / Business Management to align strategic decisions with service execution, operational resiliency, controls, and client-ready delivery.
- Provide strategic input into SLAs, KPIs, KRIs, issue tracking, executive scorecards, and operating forums so service performance and client feedback inform commercial prioritization.
- Establish a regular product governance rhythm with Finance, Operations, Technology, Risk, Relationship Management, and business-line leaders.
- Ensure strategic decisions support a scalable custody platform across Asset Managers and Corporate Trust / structured finance segments.

Risk, Controls & Regulatory Alignment
- Partner with Legal, Compliance, Risk, Operations, and Network Management to ensure custody strategy, pricing, market expansion, and new capabilities align with custody regulations, policies, risk appetite, and controls.
- Incorporate regulatory, market structure, settlement, tax, asset servicing, and sub-custodian considerations into roadmap decisions.
- Support strategy-level risk reviews, control assessments, and remediation planning where design, pricing, service standards, or operating model gaps create risk.

Financial Management & Resource Stewardship
- Partner with Finance and business leadership on forecasting, budgeting, investment prioritization, vendor / third-party cost analysis, and strategy-level financial planning.
- Ensure strategic investments are supported by clear business cases, expected financial outcomes, operational readiness requirements, and measurable benefits.
- Work with CAO / Business Management to align revenue, margin, investment progress, service quality, and issue themes into executive scorecards.

Specifications
This role operates in a matrixed, highly regulated financial services environment and requires frequent partnership with senior leaders, Strategy, Operations, Finance, Technology, Risk, Network Management, Relationship Management, clients, consultants, and external industry participants.
The role requires strong commercial judgment, custody expertise, financial discipline, strategy capability, and the ability to translate client needs, market trends, industry developments, and operational complexity into clear strategic priorities.

Basic Qualifications
- Management/supervisory experience
- 10 or more years of banking or other relevant experience

Preferred Qualifications
- 10+ years of progressive experience in custody, asset servicing, securities services, strategy, financial services strategy, or related institutional banking roles.
- Demonstrated understanding of global custody, including safekeeping, settlement, asset servicing, cash, tax, market access, sub-custodian networks, and client service delivery.
- Experience developing or managing custody strategy, pricing frameworks, business cases, roadmaps, financial performance routines, or commercial growth plans.
- Strong financial acumen with ability to analyze revenue, margin, profitability, pricing, cost drivers, and investment returns.
- Proven ability to lead through influence across Strategy, Operations, Technology, Risk, Finance, Relationship Management, clients, industry participants, and senior leadership stakeholders.
- Bachelor’s degree in finance, Business, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.
- MBA, or equivalent advanced credential.
- Experience at a global custodian, asset servicer, bank, or institutional platform with exposure to cross-border custody, fund services, Corporate Trust / structured finance, ETFs, alternatives, CLOs, or asset-manager segments.
- Experience partnering with Technology and Operations to modernize platforms, automate workflows, improve reporting, and scale strategic custody capabilities.
- Familiarity with emerging custody trends including digital assets, tokenization, T+1 settlement, blockchain-based recordkeeping, and regulatory evolution.

Competencies

Strategy & Commercial Ownership
- P&L, Pricing & Margin Discipline
- Client-Centric Product Design
- Client-Centric Strategy Design
- Investment Prioritization & Business Case Development
- Cross-Functional Influence & Executive Communication
- Data-Driven Decision Making
- Risk, Controls & Governance Discipline
- Operating Model & Transformation Orientation
- Financial Acumen and Commercial Judgment
- These competencies reflect the role’s focus on strategic ownership, commercial discipline, executive influence, client- and industry-facing engagement, and risk-aware execution.

jobs.title: Sales Support & Training Strategy Manager
jobs.description:
At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions and enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed.  We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive at every stage of your career. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.

Job Description
The Sales Support & Training Strategy Manager is an individual-contributor program manager within the Client Solutions Resources & Training team, with balanced responsibility for coordinating sales support and developing training strategy across Treasury and Payment Solutions. On the sales support side, the role equips sales teams with product expertise, compelling demonstrations, and practical tools that strengthen opportunities. On the training strategy side, the role assesses learning needs, recommends priorities, and implements scalable education approaches that build knowledge, readiness, and consistent execution across sales and client-facing teams.
Success is measured equally through the effectiveness of sales support and the impact of training strategy. Key indicators include seller readiness, demonstration quality, stakeholder satisfaction, learning adoption, knowledge retention, resource utilization, and contribution to stronger sales execution and client outcomes. The position has no direct reports and does not own a sales quota or product roadmap; it delivers results through subject matter expertise, program coordination, cross-functional influence, demonstrations, training solutions, and quantifiable client satisfaction.
The ideal candidate is a hands-on, consultative professional who combines sales support experience with training strategy, instructional design, presentation, facilitation, project coordination, and stakeholder management capabilities. This individual can simplify complex product capabilities, assess learning needs, tailor demonstrations and training solutions, manage work across multiple partners, and influence outcomes in a complex financial services or technology environment.

Key Responsibilities
Sales Support Strategy & Execution
- Coordinate and continuously improve sales support practices for Treasury and Payment Solutions, aligning resources, processes, and engagement approaches with sales priorities and opportunity needs.
- Partner with sales professionals to clarify opportunity context, define engagement goals, prepare product positioning, and anticipate questions or objections.
- Plan, prepare, and deliver tailored product demonstrations that clearly connect capabilities to prospect objectives and desired business outcomes.
- Provide product expertise, consultative guidance, and presentation support throughout the sales cycle.
- Maintain repeatable demonstration standards, discovery practices, presentation assets, and seller-readiness tools that improve consistency, quality, and scalability.

Training Strategy & Learning Solutions
- Develop and maintain a training strategy for Treasury and Payment Solutions that aligns learning priorities, curricula, resources, and delivery approaches with business objectives and workforce needs.
- Deliver engaging training through instructor-led sessions, live and recorded webinars, virtual learning environments, and other appropriate venues based on audience needs, content, and business objectives.
- Translate business and learner needs into structured learning journeys, curricula, role-based development plans, and targeted training solutions.
- Apply adult-learning and instructional-design principles to create effective instructor-led, virtual, self-directed, and blended learning experiences.
- Coordinate governance, prioritization, maintenance, and evaluation practices that keep training accurate, relevant, scalable, and aligned with changing products and business priorities.

Enablement, Learning Content & Product Expertise
- Create and maintain demonstration scripts, learning modules, facilitator guides, participant materials, product guides, job aids, assessments, and reinforcement resources.
- Coach sales and client-facing teams to conduct effective discovery, position solutions clearly, and apply product knowledge with confidence.
- Maintain deep working knowledge of Treasury and Payment Solutions products, including SinglePoint capabilities, client workflows, competitive positioning, adoption needs, and implementation considerations.
- Partner with Product teams on updates, launches, training-readiness activities, and modernization of demonstration and learning resources.
- Ensure sales enablement and training materials remain accurate, accessible, compliant, audience-centered, and aligned with approved positioning and instructional standards.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Collaboration
- Build strong partnerships across Sales, Product, Treasury Management, Operations, Implementation, Client Support, Marketing, and other client-facing teams.
- Work with subject matter experts to maintain accurate product knowledge and convert technical information into practical sales guidance and effective learning experiences.
- Coach and support colleagues who contribute to sales enablement, product demonstrations, instructional design, facilitation, or training delivery, without direct supervisory responsibility.

Measurement & Continuous Improvement
- Establish balanced measures for sales support effectiveness and training impact, including seller readiness, demonstration quality, stakeholder satisfaction, participation, learning adoption, knowledge retention, resource utilization, and performance improvement.
- Use sales partner feedback, learner feedback, assessment results, utilization data, and business outcomes to refine strategy, content, and delivery practices.
- Identify patterns across sales opportunities and learning needs and recommend improvements to product positioning, enablement resources, curricula, demonstrations, and cross-functional processes.
- Scale sales support and training practices while maintaining accuracy, consistency, responsiveness, instructional quality, and a strong learner experience.

Basic Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree, or equivalent work experience
- Eight to ten years of experience in project management activities

Preferred Skills/Experience
- Bachelor's degree in Business, Communications, Marketing, Education, Instructional Design, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
- 5+ years of experience spanning sales enablement, presales support, training strategy, instructional design, product demonstrations, facilitation, or related disciplines.
- Demonstrated experience supporting sales opportunities and developing product, role-based, or departmental training strategies.
- Ability to conduct effective discovery and learning needs assessments and translate findings into tailored demonstrations, curricula, and training solutions.
- Strong facilitation, presentation, storytelling, instructional design, project management, strategic thinking, and stakeholder management skills.
- Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex concepts clearly and credibly.
- Ability to independently manage multiple opportunities, training initiatives, deliverables, and priorities in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment.
- Experience within financial services, treasury management, payments, banking, fintech, or business-to-business technology.
- Experience supporting complex sales cycles and coordinating product, role-based, or departmental learning programs.
- Knowledge of treasury management platforms, payment workflows, client onboarding, and related operational considerations.
- Experience creating scalable demonstration, sales enablement, curriculum, or blended-learning programs.
- Experience measuring sales support and training effectiveness through feedback, assessments, analytics, knowledge retention, performance indicators, and business outcomes.
- Experience coaching presenters, facilitators, sales professionals, or other client-facing colleagues through influence rather than formal supervision.

jobs.description:

Job Description
Lead strategy. Strengthen partnerships. Shape the future of global custody.

Are you a strategic financial services leader who can turn complex client and business needs into meaningful results? Join us as a Strategic Services Operations Manager and help advance a global custody platform through executive partnership, operational leadership, and cross-functional execution.

In this highly visible role, you will serve as a strategic bridge between business partners, clients, and operations. You will collaborate across Wealth, Global Fund Services, Institutional Trust & Custody, Corporate Trust, Product, Technology, Risk, Finance, and other key organizations to translate emerging needs into actionable initiatives and service enhancements.

What You'll Do
- Build trusted relationships with senior leaders, clients, relationship managers, product partners, and operational teams.
- Lead executive engagement routines, governance forums, strategic reporting, and service-level agreement oversight.
- Coordinate the identification, escalation, tracking, and resolution of complex custody-related issues.
- Translate client feedback, market developments, and operational challenges into strategic initiatives, product enhancements, and measurable business outcomes.
- Provide custody market expertise through client presentations, business reviews, industry analysis, and strategic consultations.
- Partner with business development and relationship management teams to support client retention, growth opportunities, and complex client needs.
- Drive cross-functional initiatives involving Operations, Product, Technology, Risk, Finance, Legal, and Compliance.
- Help internal teams and clients prepare for regulatory, market, and operational changes.
- Represent the organization with clients, investment managers, sub-custodians, fintech providers, and industry participants.

Why Top Talent is Excited About This Opportunity
This is more than an operations leadership role. You'll serve as a trusted advisor to senior leaders, influence strategic decisions, champion the voice of the client, and help shape the future of a growing global custody business. Your expertise will directly impact client satisfaction, operational excellence, product evolution, and business growth.
You'll have the opportunity to:
- Influence enterprise-wide initiatives and strategic priorities.
- Partner with executive leadership across multiple business lines.
- Drive meaningful change in a complex, highly visible environment.
- Support major institutional clients and sophisticated market participants.
- Serve as a recognized subject matter expert and industry ambassador.

The Ideal Candidate
You are a strategic thinker, relationship builder, and trusted business partner who thrives in complex environments. You understand the evolving custody landscape, anticipate client and business needs, and bring people together to solve problems, improve outcomes, and drive growth. You are equally comfortable in executive boardrooms, client meetings, governance forums, and cross-functional working sessions.

Location : 3+ days onsite in New Jersey or Saint Paul

What You Bring
Basic Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Operations Management, or a related discipline.
- 10+ years of experience in Global Custody, Asset Servicing, Corporate Trust, Institutional Banking, Operations, Client Service, Business Engagement, Relationship Management, or related financial services functions.

Preferred Skills/Experience

- Direct experience within Global Custody Services, Asset Servicing, Securities Processing, Institutional Trust & Custody, or Corporate Trust.
- Strong network within the institutional custody and asset servicing industry.
- Experience supporting strategic growth initiatives, client retention efforts, and business development activities.
- Proven ability to influence operating models, product strategies, and client service frameworks across a large financial institution.
- Deep understanding of global custody services, asset servicing, securities processing, cash correspondent banking, and complex asset administration.
- Experience supporting institutional and wealth-focused business lines within a large financial institution.
- Proven ability to build executive-level partnerships and influence senior stakeholders.
- Strong experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives and driving results without direct authority.
- Expertise in issue management, governance, service delivery, and operational improvement.
- Exceptional communication, presentation, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to successfully manage competing priorities in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
- Strong leadership capabilities with a focus on collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.

jobs.title: Head of Strategic Finance & Resource Allocation
jobs.description:
At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions and enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed.  We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. Job Description
U.S. Bank is seeking a Head of Strategic Finance & Resource Allocation, a senior executive to build and lead enterprise capability for forward-looking financial strategy and resource allocation decisions. This role provides decision support that guides strategic priorities, aligns investment choices with long-term value creation, and partners to ensure capital and resources are deployed against the enterprise’s highest-priority opportunities.

Essential Functions
- Frame and influence enterprise trade-offs across capital, cost structure, and growth investments, serving as trusted counsel on MC- and BOD-ready decision inputs and narratives.
- Guide enterprise capital allocation and resource allocation analysis across growth, cost, risk, and balance sheet priorities, extensively partnering with relevant stakeholders.
- Provide forward-looking enterprise decision support to guide strategic priorities, resource deployment, and executive decision-making.
- Leverage enterprise quantitative models, scenario analysis, sensitivity analysis, and external risk perspectives to inform assumptions, options, and recommendations.
- Deliver flexible and agile analytics solutions deployed to priority strategic problems, investment decisions, and emerging strategic questions.
- In concert with Enterprise Strategy, provide strategic financial partnership to guide strategic initiatives and enterprise decision forums.
- Deliver MC- and BOD-ready competitive and strategic financial insights, decision framing, executive materials, and recommendations that clarify choices, trade-offs, and implications.
- Synthesize competitive performance, market intelligence, economic context, and external risk perspectives into enterprise strategic insight.
- Translate external and competitive insight into capital allocation, enterprise trade‑offs, and strategic priorities.

What Success Looks Like
- Trusted decision partner to the Managing Committee, CFO, and CEO — extending influence of Corporate FP&A on enterprise and BOD matters
- Forward-looking, scenario-based decision support is consistently used to guide enterprise priorities and leadership decisions.
- Resource allocation choices are transparent, strategy-aligned, and grounded in clear trade-off analysis.
- Executive teams spend more time making decisions and less time reconciling assumptions, options, or financial implications.
- Priority strategic questions receive timely, agile analytics support that clarifies choices and accelerates action.
- Competitive and external insight are embedded enterprise strategic choices that clearly connect strategy, financial outcomes, risks, and recommended actions.

Preferred Skills/Experience
- Deep financial analysis, enterprise FP&A, capital allocation, and resource allocation expertise.
- Strong executive decision-framing skills, including the ability to translate complex analysis into clear choices, trade-offs, and recommendations.
- Experience leveraging scenario modeling, sensitivity analysis, stress testing, and external risk perspectives to inform strategic decisions.
- Strategic vision and enterprise orientation, with the judgment to balance growth, cost, risk, and balance sheet priorities.
- Proven ability to build collaborative relationships across Finance, Enterprise Strategy, business lines, and executive leadership forums.
- Strong communication and executive presence, including experience developing MC- and BOD-ready materials.
- Demonstrated ability to build, lead, and scale high-performing analytical teams.
- MBA, CFA, or equivalent advanced finance, strategy, or quantitative credentials.
- Experience spanning both strategy and finance, ideally in an enterprise or corporate finance leadership capacity.
- Experience leading capital allocation, strategic finance, or resource allocation functions at a large financial institution.
- Familiarity with bank balance sheet dynamics, regulatory expectations, economic outlooks, and enterprise risk considerations.

Job Description
U.S. Bank’s Institutional Client Group (ICG) cultivates clients’ trust through customized service and access to the bank’s resources and expertise. Through a One U.S. Bank approach, ICG brings together capabilities across capital markets, credit, payments, liquidity, investments, and other financial solutions to help corporate clients achieve their strategic, financial and operational objectives. ICG Global Industrials and Services (GIS) serves large corporate clients with more than $1 billion in annual revenue that are not covered by one of U.S. Bank’s Specialized Industries divisions. The organization operates through a region-based coverage model designed to align senior bankers with client needs, markets, and growth opportunities.

U.S. Bank is seeking an experienced senior corporate banking leader to serve as a Division Manager for the GIS Northeast division. This position will provide strategic direction and oversight for the Northeast large-cap corporate banking business, leading a team of experienced Relationship Managers and relationship management professionals responsible for developing and expanding relationships with sophisticated corporate clients. The Division Manager will be accountable for the overall growth, performance, and strategic direction of the division. The leader will establish market and client priorities, drive business development efforts, deepen existing relationships, and position the team to capture significant new opportunities with large corporate clients. Particular emphasis will be placed on identifying priority clients and prospects, expanding U.S. Bank’s relevance with clients, and pursuing opportunities where the bank can take meaningful leadership roles.

Base pay for this role usually falls within $275,000 to $315,000.  Additional considerations regarding base pay levels are based on candidate qualifications. Your compensation expectations will be discussed with a U.S. Bank recruiter if you are contacted to discuss the role further.

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in finance, accounting, business or other related field
- 15 or more years of banking experience

- Extensive knowledge of large corporate banking and the financial needs of companies with revenues exceeding $1 billion
- Proven ability to establish and execute a strategic business-development plan and drive sustainable revenue and relationship growth
- Strong track record of originating new relationships and expanding existing client relationships
- Executive presence and demonstrated ability to develop trusted relationships with senior corporate executives and financial decision makers
- Advanced knowledge of corporate credit, complex financing structures, capital structures and risk management
- Ability to identify, prioritize and pursue significant client and prospect opportunities
- Demonstrated ability to lead senior Relationship Managers and create a high-performance, accountable and collaborative team culture
- Strong coaching, talent development, and leadership capabilities

- Strong understanding of capital markets, treasury management, payments and other corporate banking solutions
- Ability to balance relationship growth, credit quality, risk management, and profitability
- Strong negotiation and influencing skills with senior internal and external stakeholders
- Excellent analytical, strategic decision-making and problem-solving skills
- Excellent verbal, written and executive-level communication skills
- Considerable tact, diplomacy and interpersonal skills

Job Description
U.S. Bank is seeking a Merger & Acquisitions Technology Director. The M&A Technology Integration Director will serve as the primary technology integration leader for mergers, acquisitions, and divestitures, accountable for end‑to‑end technology integration strategy, execution, and value realization while ensuring regulatory, risk, and security expectations are met. The Integration Lead acts as the single point of accountability across technology workstreams from due diligence through separation or full integration.

Key Responsibilities
- Lead technology due diligence activities for mergers, acquisitions, and divestitures, assessing applications, infrastructure, data, cybersecurity, identity management, and third-party dependencies.
- Develop and execute technology integration and separation strategies, including full integrations, carve-outs, TSA-based transitions, and stand-alone operating models.
- Serve as the single point of accountability for all technology integration workstreams from due diligence through Day-1 readiness, stabilization, and final transition.
- Drive cross-functional collaboration across Technology, Security, Risk, Compliance, Legal, Privacy, Operations, and external partners to ensure successful transaction outcomes.
- Establish and maintain Day-1 operational readiness, including user access, infrastructure connectivity, collaboration tools, security controls, and business continuity requirements.
- Manage integration budgets, forecasts, resource plans, vendor engagements, and technology investment requests while tracking costs against deal assumptions.
- Identify, assess, and mitigate technology, regulatory, operational, and cybersecurity risks, ensuring compliance with enterprise policies and audit requirements.
- Prepare and present executive-level updates, governance materials, risk assessments, and strategic recommendations to sponsors, leadership teams, and investment committees.

Technology Due Diligence & Deal Assessment
- Lead comprehensive technology due diligence for acquisitions and divestitures, including applications, infrastructure, data, identity and access, security, and third‑party dependencies.
- Assess integration complexity, cost, risk, and feasibility to inform deal decision‑making.
- Develop technology estimates, assumptions, and risk assessments in partnership with internal and external stakeholders.
- Identify technology constraints, dependencies, and potential deal risks; drive early mitigation strategies.

Integration & Separation Strategy
- Define the end‑to‑end technology integration or separation strategy aligned to deal intent (e.g., full integration, stand‑alone, carve‑out, TSA‑based, or hybrid models).
- Own creation and approval of the Technology Integration Approach, including target and transition states, sequencing, and exit criteria.
- Balance speed‑to‑value objectives with security, regulatory, and operational requirements.
- Tailor integration approaches based on transaction size, complexity, and regulatory posture.

Execution Leadership
- Serve as the primary technology integration lead accountable for delivery across all technology workstreams.
- Coordinate and direct cross‑functional technology teams, system integrators, and vendors.
- Manage interdependencies, resolve conflicts, and drive decision‑making to maintain timelines and outcomes.
- Ensure execution progresses smoothly from pre‑close through Day‑1 readiness, stabilization, and completion.

Day‑1 & Regulatory Readiness
- Ensure technology readiness for Day‑1 operations, including user access, collaboration, infrastructure connectivity, and security controls.
- Define stand‑alone operating boundaries and interim control models where required.
- Coordinate legal, regulatory, and approval‑driven dependencies impacting close or Day‑1 operations.
- Ensure required documentation, approvals, and evidence are in place to support audits and regulatory review.

Risk, Security & Compliance
- Embed enterprise risk, data protection, and security principles throughout the integration or separation lifecycle.
- Partner with Technology Risk, Data Protection & Privacy, Identity, and Security teams to ensure policy and control alignment.
- Own planning and execution of remediation activities for integration‑related findings or risk issues.
- Maintain appropriate evidence and documentation to support internal and external audits.

Financial & Resource Management
- Develop and manage technology integration budgets, forecasts, and investment requests.
- Support resourcing decisions, including headcount justification and vendor sourcing.
- Track technology costs against deal assumptions and escalate variances as appropriate.

Stakeholder & Executive Communication
- Act as the primary technology contact for deal sponsors, executive leadership, and integration governance forums.
- Provide clear, concise status reporting, risk updates, and decision points to senior leaders.
- Prepare and present executive‑level materials for investment committees, management committees, and governance reviews.
- Proactively escalate issues that could impact deal value, timeline, or compliance.

Divestiture & Separation Execution
- Lead end‑to‑end technology separation efforts, including data carveouts, system disentanglement, TSA management, and decommissioning.
- Define and manage TSA exit criteria and timelines.
- Ensure secure transition, data handling, and shutdown activities are completed in accordance with legal and regulatory requirements.

Continuous Improvement & Leadership
- Contribute to the development and refinement of M&A technology integration standards, playbooks, and methodologies.
- Identify opportunities to improve repeatability, speed, quality, and risk outcomes across deals.
- Mentor integration managers and project managers supporting M&A initiatives.
- Capture and share lessons learned to strengthen enterprise M&A capabilities.

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
- 8+ years of experience in technology leadership roles, including significant experience supporting mergers, acquisitions, and/or divestitures.
- Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross‑functional technology initiatives.
- Strong understanding of enterprise technology environments, security, risk, and regulatory considerations.
- Proven executive communication and stakeholder management skills.

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience in regulated industries (e.g., financial services).
- Prior experience leading technology integrations or separations with significant regulatory oversight.
- Familiarity with integration governance models, TSAs, and carveout execution.

Key Competencies
- Strategic thinking and decision‑making.
- Executive communication and influence.

- Risk and compliance awareness.

Are you energized by helping people get good at something? Do you enjoy turning a complicated tool into something a person can use with confidence? U.S. Bank is seeking a collaborative and creative analyst to own training and user enablement for the ARES platform and help our users get real value from it.

Why this role matters
A platform is only as good as its users' ability to use it well. This role owns the entire experience of learning ARES, from a new user's first session to the resources they turn to six months in. You will create the training, run the forums where users bring their questions, lead the champion network that carries knowledge into the business lines, and serve as a direct line between what users struggle with and what the platform team builds next. Your work is what turns a capable platform into an adopted one.

What you will do
- Create and maintain ARES training content, including training videos, user guides, job aids, and reference materials

- Build and maintain reporting on training completion, adoption, user sentiment, and engagement, and present findings to management

Domo, Microsoft SharePoint, Microsoft 365 (Teams, Outlook, PowerPoint, Excel, Forms), video creation and editing tools, and survey and reporting platforms.

What makes this opportunity exciting
You will own the full user experience of a platform that matters to the business, build a user feedback program from the ground up and see your recommendations shape the roadmap, and lead a champion network that extends your reach across multiple business lines. This is a highly visible role with direct exposure to Product, Technology, Operations, and business line leadership, on a team that is actively building its operating model rather than maintaining someone else's.

Users know where to go for answers and find them. Training is current, engaging, and matched to how people really work. The champion network is active rather than nominal. Leadership has clear visibility into user sentiment and adoption, with a feedback loop that visibly closes so users can see that what they said produced change.

Marketing Data Strategy & Operating Model

- Set portfolio priorities and investment strategies that maximize business impact, improve marketing effectiveness, and accelerate data-driven decision-making.
- Partner across Marketing, Analytics, Data, Technology, and Business leadership teams to shape and execute the future-state marketing data and analytics strategy.

Job Description
The Fraud Analytics Risk Analyst supports U.S. Bank’s Enterprise Fraud Risk organization by delivering the analysis that recurring reporting cannot. This analyst investigates fraud losses, claims, complaints, and operational data to identify root causes and emerging risk trends, and provides independent, data-driven credible challenge to business line fraud strategies, processes, and controls.

Core Responsibilities

- Perform independent, data-driven analyses of fraud losses, claims, complaints, alerts, operational data, and other risk indicators to identify root causes, control gaps, emerging fraud risks, and customer impacts.
- Provide effective second-line credible challenge to business line fraud strategies, detection rules, controls, processes, and performance reporting through analytical deep dives and independent assessments.
- Develop independent benchmarks, thresholds, segmentation frameworks, key risk indicators, and trend analyses to assess changes in fraud exposure, control effectiveness, customer outcomes, and loss performance.
- Design and maintain transparent, repeatable, and auditable analytical methodologies, monitoring frameworks, and governance processes that can be independently validated, refreshed, and reproduced as new data becomes available.
- Proactively identify emerging fraud threats, control weaknesses, and monitoring opportunities by sourcing and analyzing relevant data assets, developing actionable insights, and recommending risk mitigation actions to business and risk management stakeholders.
- Assess the fraud risk implications of significant business, product, strategy, model, vendor, and technology changes through independent impact analyses and provide risk-based recommendations
- Support strategic data and cloud modernization initiatives involving fraud analytics, monitoring solutions, reporting assets, and analytical controls, including migration to Databricks, Azure, cloud data platforms, and enterprise data domains.

Basic Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree, or equivalent work experience
- Typically more than six years of applicable experience

Preferred Skills and Experience

- Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative field, or equivalent work experience

- Four or more years of experience in analytics, risk management, fraud, financial crimes, or a related field

- Experience querying relational databases and working with large data sets from multiple sources

- Proficiency in at least one analytical language or platform (SAS, SQL, Python, R, or similar), with the flexibility to learn new tools

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including presenting findings to a business audience

- Experience with fraud, scams, payments, claims, complaints, or operational risk data in financial services

- Experience working with unstructured or free-text data and building categorization logic

- Experience providing credible challenge or independent risk oversight

- Experience with Power BI, Tableau, or similar visualization tools; interest in Databricks and cloud analytics platforms

- Comfort using AI tools such as Microsoft Copilot within an analytical workflow

Job Description
Reporting to the Head of Consumer & Business Banking Foreign Exchange (CBB FX), the FX Business Development Officer will play a critical role in driving the growth and expansion of U.S. Bank's Foreign Exchange business across Consumer Banking, Emerging and Affluent Wealth, Small Business Banking, and Business Banking client segments.
This position combines business development, sales execution, relationship management, and partner engagement responsibilities. The successful candidate will be responsible for identifying, qualifying, and developing foreign exchange opportunities while supporting senior FX sales professionals in delivering tailored solutions to clients and prospects with international banking needs.
A primary focus of the role will be proactively building a pipeline of new business opportunities through partner referrals, internal prospecting tools, outbound calling efforts, and direct client engagement. The FX Business Development Officer will work closely with Branch Managers, Wealth Advisors, Small Business Specialists, Business Bankers, Treasury Payments Consultants, and other key partners to expand awareness of FX capabilities, uncover international payment needs, and increase adoption of foreign exchange products and services across the franchise.
This role is ideal for a highly motivated sales professional seeking to build a career in foreign exchange sales, international payments, and relationship management while contributing directly to revenue growth and client acquisition efforts

Key Responsibilities:
Business Development & Sales Generation
- Prospect and develop new FX opportunities across Consumer, Wealth, Small Business, and Business Banking segments through internal referrals, portfolio reviews, market intelligence, and outbound sales activities.

- Build and maintain a robust pipeline of prospective clients with cross-border payment, foreign currency, and international banking needs.

- Identify opportunities among clients involved in international trade, overseas real estate transactions, foreign investments, international education expenses, family support payments, and other global financial activities.

- Conduct outbound calling campaigns and business development initiatives designed to generate qualified opportunities and expand FX penetration.

- Support efforts to acquire both new-to-bank relationships and deepen existing client relationships through additional FX and international payment solutions.

Client Engagement & Sales Support
- Participate in client meetings, discovery calls, and sales presentations alongside senior FX sales professionals.

- Engage directly with clients to understand international business and personal banking needs, identify opportunities, and present appropriate FX solutions.

- Assist with the sales process from opportunity identification through transaction execution and relationship expansion.

- Support foreign exchange transactions, including spot contracts, forward contracts, currency orders, and cross-border payment solutions.

- Help coordinate onboarding activities, documentation requirements, product implementation, and trade readiness efforts.

Partner Development & Channel Management
- Build strong relationships with branch leadership, wealth advisors, business bankers, small business specialists, and treasury partners.

- Increase awareness of foreign exchange solutions across referral channels through ongoing education, training, and joint calling efforts.

- Assist in developing and executing partner engagement strategies designed to increase referral activity and FX market penetration.

- Deliver presentations, market updates, and educational sessions that help partners identify clients with international banking needs.

- Support regional and national initiatives focused on expanding FX capabilities throughout the Consumer, Affluent Wealth, and Small and Business Banking organization.

Market Knowledge & Advisory Support
- Develop expertise in foreign exchange markets, currency trends, international payment solutions, and global economic developments.

- Monitor market activity and communicate relevant foreign exchange insights to clients and internal partners.

- Explain foreign exchange products and market developments in a clear, practical manner that supports client decision-making.

- Stay informed on industry trends, competitive offerings, and emerging international payment opportunities.

Client Service & Operational Support
- Coordinate with Trading, Operations, Treasury Management, Credit, Compliance, and Legal teams to ensure seamless client onboarding, execution and support.

- Assist with transaction processing, payment investigations, client service requests, and issue resolution.

- Maintain accurate client records, opportunity tracking, pipeline reporting, and CRM documentation.

- Ensure all activities are conducted in accordance with U.S. Bank policies, regulatory requirements, and risk management standards.

Required

- 5+ years of experience in Foreign Exchange, Treasury Management, Wealth Management, Business Banking, Retail Banking, or Financial Services sales.

- Demonstrated ability to prospect, onboard and develop relationships, and generate new business opportunities.

- Understanding of foreign exchange markets, international payments, and cross-border banking solutions.

- Strong communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills.

- Ability to effectively engage both clients and internal business partners.

- Strong organizational and analytical skills with experience using Excel, CRM platforms, and sales pipeline management tools.

Preferred
- Experience selling or supporting foreign exchange, treasury management, payments, or international banking solutions.

- Knowledge of Spot FX, Forward Contracts, Cross-Border Payments, Currency Orders, and related products.

- Experience working with branch networks, wealth management teams, small business bankers, or commercial banking partners.

- Knowledge of CRM platforms, Power BI, and lead generation lists

- Proven success generating opportunities through prospecting, referral development, and relationship-based sales.

The ideal candidate is a highly motivated sales professional with a strong business development mindset and a passion for helping clients navigate international financial needs. This individual possesses a hunter mentality, thrives on prospecting and pipeline development, and is energized by identifying new opportunities, building trusted relationships, and contributing directly to revenue growth. Job Description
Our Commercial Real Estate team
Commercial Real Estate (CRE) is recruiting for its next Credit Analyst class to join the National CRE Underwriting Team. This selective program provides a diverse foundation in commercial real estate and credit principles. Analysts gather, analyze, and interpret loan information to assess performance and recommend actions to address risk. The program offers a collaborative and fast-paced environment while preparing candidates for internal opportunities in Relationship Management, Capital Markets, Underwriting Management, Technology / Analytics, and Credit.
Credit analysts are located in seven regional underwriting offices supporting approximately 30 origination offices throughout the country. U.S. Bank’s Commercial Real Estate platform is one of the largest in the United States. We deliver a comprehensive set of financing solutions to institutional, public, and private commercial real estate investors, including lines of credit (working capital, subscription, repurchase) and project debt (construction, bridge, term) to acquire, construct or rehab property types including multifamily, industrial, office, retail and more.

What you’ll do
Conduct analysis of financial statements and assessment of credit requests, providing recommendations tied to analysis and assessment of credit risk. Over the course of our 3-year program, you will receive accelerated learning and skill development through a mix of formal training, mentorship, and a community of peers and advisors.

As a CRE Analyst, you’ll:
- Underwrite new business opportunities for credit approval, including project, market, and sponsor financial analysis, structuring of loan terms, and risk evaluation.

- Monitor existing loan portfolios, including market analysis, covenant compliance tracking, collection and analysis of financial statements, problem loan reporting, and ongoing assessment of risk factors that may affect a project’s and/or client’s risk profile.

- Measure, monitor, and test a wide variety of financial covenants as specified within credit approval documents

- Read and interpret relevant credit approval requirements to accurately input monitoring requirements and covenants into a standard compliance monitoring system

- Analyze financial statement results and prepare reports to communicate financial performance and trends with Portfolio Managers, Relationship Managers, and/or Credit Administration

- Interact with clients as appropriate; attend meetings or calls with companies in the supported portfolio

- Develop technical and business acumen through training, mentorship, and exposure to senior executives

- Build a supportive community of peers through a variety of cohort strengthening activities such as social events, volunteer days, and development workshops

- Utilize AI-enabled tools, including Microsoft Copilot, to support financial analysis, market research, portfolio monitoring, and preparation of credit-related materials while applying appropriate professional judgment and risk discipline.

We’re looking for talent with demonstrated leadership capabilities, strong work ethic and intellectual curiosity.

- Proficient in Excel and PowerPoint

Great leaders aren't born in a classroom, but the right learning experience helps them get there faster. As a Leadership Development Facilitator, you'll create learning experiences that help leaders at every level lead with clarity, candor and confidence. That includes new people managers through senior executives.
You'll lead workshops in person and virtually. You'll partner with business line executives to understand what their leaders need. You'll also help shape solutions that build capability across the enterprise. This role is for a facilitator who can consult, design and deliver, not only present.

What you'll do

- Lead high-impact leadership experiences. Facilitate enterprise programs and custom leader sessions in person and virtually. Topics range from foundational management skills to executive-level team development.
- Bring presence to every room. Build trust quickly, handle complex conversations with composure, and adjust in the moment when leaders push back or discussions go off-script.
- Partner with executives and HR leaders. Work with senior stakeholders to diagnose needs, recommend the right solution, and connect the learning to business strategy and outcomes.
- Shape learning solutions. Contribute to needs analysis, design and enhancement. Influence facilitator guides, activities and debriefs so programs land with leaders.

- Proven experience facilitating leadership or management development, ideally with senior leader or executive audiences
- Strong executive presence and the credibility to challenge leaders' thinking respectfully
- Skill in leading conversations about feedback, accountability, coaching and change
- Business acumen: you can connect learning to strategy, performance and results
- Experience consulting with stakeholders and contributing to learning design
- Comfort using data and feedback to drive continuous improvement
- Fluency in virtual facilitation tools and engaging hybrid delivery

jobs.description:

Job Description
The Commercial Real Estate Senior Underwriter manages portfolio risk by ensuring timeliness and accuracy of all credit actions, by providing guidance on credit structure and risk rating decisions and by participating in pre-flight discussions. Coordinates work with Credit, Loan Administration and other groups, promoting consistent quality and conciseness of credit documents and streamlining workflow among underwriting, credit approval and loan administration.

Underwriting & Credit Analysis
- Underwrite new originations and portfolio exposures for a broad range of CRE asset classes.
- Analyze borrower financials, property cash flows, collateral valuation, sponsor strength, covenant sensitivities, and market conditions
- Prepare clear, comprehensive written credit analyses and supporting documentation
- Execute straightforward credit requests for existing clients with limited supervision
- Assist with annual company‑wide credit reviews for clients with multiple property holdings, including analysis beyond bank‑financed properties

Transaction & Deal Support
- Support both existing property transactions (including refinancings) and ground‑up construction projects, including budget monitoring and monthly construction draw reviews through project completion
- Assist with new deal originations, evaluating opportunities with typical transaction sizes of $50MM–$100MM, with select transactions up to $750MM
- Participate in the preparation and negotiation of term sheets, as applicable

Portfolio Management & Credit Monitoring
- Support Relationship Managers and Portfolio Managers in managing an assigned portfolio of commercial real estate client relationships
- Perform accurate and consistent spreading of borrower financial statements in accordance with bank standards and credit policies
- Prepare quarterly trend analyses, monitoring reports, and covenant compliance testing
- Maintain compliance monitoring and financial reporting databases, including tracking credit agreement requirements, borrower financial receipt, and key credit metrics
- Participate in quarterly portfolio reviews, including analysis of operating statements, rent rolls, and risk assessments
- Proactively identify and communicate emerging risks, mitigants, and other issues at the transaction and portfolio level

Collaboration & Communication
- Collaborate effectively with Credit Approvers and internal risk partners
- Participate in client bank meetings, as needed, to support underwriting, portfolio management, and risk discussions
- Serve as a reliable first line of credit analysis, escalating issues appropriately

Basic Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree, or equivalent work experience
- Five or more years of commercial lending experience

Preferred Skills/Experience
- Strong foundation in CRE underwriting across multiple property types (cash flow, valuation, sponsor analysis, structure, and covenants).
- Experience authoring credit memoranda and presenting key risks, mitigants, and recommendations to approval committees
- Strong analytical and technical writing skills; able to translate complex sponsor/tenant/technical diligence into clear credit narratives
- Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across origination, portfolio management, credit risk, and technical advisors
- Comfort operating with accountability—independently driving analyses while partnering closely with Relationship Managers, Portfolio Managers, and Credit Approvers
- Familiarity with banking credit policy, loan documentation concepts, and CRE underwriting processes (construction, bridge, term, and portfolio facilities)
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel (cash flow modeling and scenario analysis) and the broader Microsoft Office Suite
- Experience with nCino, CoStar, and/or other CRE platforms preferred

Our qualification review for this role considers the totality of a candidate’s background, including relevant work experience, education, military experience, and specialized training. Equivalent combinations of these experiences may satisfy the minimum qualifications for the role.

This role requires working from a U.S. Bank location three (3) or more days per week. This position is located in Charlotte, NC, and New York, NY.

- Lead the implementation and maintenance of the USBE Corporate Compliance and Risk assessment framework for the UK branch;

- Assist in the deployment and operation of the Bank’s Compliance and Conduct Risk  programs including but not exclusively regulatory change, risk and compliance assessments, rtc;

Credit Strategy is a dynamic team within Credit Risk Management focused on optimizing the identification, quantification and mitigation of credit risk. The team oversees critical second line of defense risk management programs including USB’s risk limit framework, risk rating, policy exceptions, risk ID, credit concentration, stress testing, collateral audit, credit policy and procedures, portfolio monitoring, strategic product growth and/or enhancements, regulatory review and compliance, and rapid response to emerging risk. Credit Strategy culture revolves around innovation, execution and collaboration across all 3 lines of defense and regulatory bodies. Talent seeking to join the Strategy team should possess an inquisitive and growth mindset, track record of taking initiative, and agility to problem solve in a team setting.

About the Role
In this role, you will serve as a thought leader, coordinator and implementation manager to help ensure we effectively meet or exceed the goals for key credit risk management strategy initiatives and programs.

Industry Credit Risk Management – Officer is responsible for portfolio management of specific industries and products portfolios across U.S. Bank (including, by not limited to, Asset Based Finance, Equipment Finance, Mortgage Warehouse Lending). The functions include emerging risk identification, managing risk appetite through risk limits and credit policies, portfolio construction and asset allocation strategies, as well as management of concentration, correlation, and specialized risks associated with the portfolios. Additional duties would include developing pro-active and forward-looking viewpoints regarding the industry / portfolio and creating solutions and recommendations for managing risk and influencing positive change.  This includes directing, monitoring, and coordinating risk management projects for assigned industries / portfolios.  This role provides independent risk management and governance while working closely with the business line, credit approval and various other key constituents to build out a comprehensive and proactive approach to portfolio management that promotes a strong risk management culture, aligned with U.S. Bank’s risk appetite.

You will build and maintain relationships with peers in the Credit Strategy as well as the broader Credit Risk Management (CRM) organization and line of business to achieve desired project goals or program outcomes. This is an influential individual contributor role that requires managing projects simultaneously, maintaining strong procedural documentation, and adjusting priorities as the business and regulatory environment evolves.

Key Activities
- Partnering with Credit Risk Management and U.S. Bank business units to identify and manage emerging risks associated with the respective portfolio. This includes developing relevant metrics and segmentation to assess exposure at risk and credit policies to mitigate short-term and long-term risks, with demonstrated value creation where feasible.

- Assisting in developing requirements for technology projects to gather relevant data and design ongoing or ad-hoc analyses as needed.

- Working with the centralized reporting team to develop and maintain relevant reporting, risk limits and analysis, and performing scenario analysis to understand the bank’s exposure to potential risks and opportunities.

- Preparing management reports and presentations to communicate current state and progress on credit-focused initiatives.

- Hands-on leader who excels at collaborating across functional areas to develop, drive and maintain the credit risk strategy and ensure we meet core business objectives

Our Business Banking Relationship Managers combine sales expertise, relationship management, and financial acumen to help business clients achieve their goals.

By developing new client relationships, deepening existing partnerships, and delivering tailored financial solutions, you'll play a key role in helping businesses thrive while growing your own career.

In this role, you'll serve as a trusted advisor to business owners, connecting them with lending, treasury management, deposit, payment, merchant services, and credit card solutions that support every stage of growth.
Backed by a team of specialists and a full suite of industry-leading products, you'll have the resources and support needed to deliver meaningful results for your clients and your portfolio.

If you're energized by building relationships, driving business growth, and making a real impact in your community, we'd love to connect with you. This position will require consistent outbound marketing activity including cold calling, attending networking events, etc.
