At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions and enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed.  We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive at every stage of your career. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.

Job Description
Our Business Banking Relationship Managers combine sales expertise, relationship management, and financial acumen to help business clients achieve their goals.
By developing new client relationships, deepening existing partnerships, and delivering tailored financial solutions, you'll play a key role in helping businesses thrive while growing your own career.
In this role, you'll serve as a trusted advisor to business owners, connecting them with lending, treasury management, deposit, payment, merchant services, and credit card solutions that support every stage of growth.
Backed by a team of specialists and a full suite of industry-leading products, you'll have the resources and support needed to deliver meaningful results for your clients and your portfolio.

If you're energized by building relationships, driving business growth, and making a real impact in your community, we'd love to connect with you. This position will require consistent outbound marketing activity including cold calling, attending networking events etc.

**U.S. Bank offers a robust, market-leading Business Banking compensation plan that rewards the full scope of your relationship-building efforts, from loan generation and deposit growth to fee-based production.

**This role may offer a sign-on bonus of up to $25,000, depending on qualifications and business considerations.

Key Responsibilities
- Spend approximately 60-70% of your time focused on outside business development, active prospecting, self-sourcing business opportunities, and building a book of business from the ground up.

- Develop, grow, and manage new and existing business client relationships.

- Build and maintain Centers of Influence (COI) networks to generate referrals and new business opportunities.

- Deliver financial expertise and client-focused solutions that create long-term, trusted relationships.

- Assess clients' banking needs and provide tailored recommendations based on their goals and objectives.

- Educate clients on available deposit, lending, treasury management, payment, and other banking solutions.

- Proactively manage an assigned portfolio by maintaining strong credit quality and overseeing renewals, annual reviews, and ongoing client needs.

- Obtain credit approval within assigned lending limits and recommend appropriate credit structures.

- Partner with Treasury Management, Merchant Services, Business Banking Credit Card, and other internal teams to deliver comprehensive financial solutions.

- Make referrals to additional business lines and specialists as appropriate to meet client needs.

Why U.S. Bank?
At U.S. Bank, you'll have access to a comprehensive suite of products, industry-leading resources, and dedicated specialist support that allow you to help clients succeed while building a rewarding and successful career.
If you're ready to maximize your earning potential, grow your portfolio, and make a meaningful impact in the communities you serve, we encourage you to apply.

Basic Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree, or equivalent work experience
- Five to seven years of relevant experience

Preferred Skills/Experience
- Experience prospecting and developing relationships with businesses generating $10MM+ in annual revenue.

- Proven success growing a portfolio through business development and consultative sales.

- Established COI network or demonstrated ability to build one.

- Commercial lending experience, including C&I, SBA, and Commercial Real Estate.

- Experience managing complex credit transactions and loan structures.

- Strong knowledge of commercial credit, portfolio management, and risk assessment.

- Excellent communication, presentation, and relationship management skills.

- Ability to collaborate effectively across business lines and partner teams.

- Strong problem-solving skills and sound business judgment in a fast-paced environment.

Location
If not meeting with clients, this role requires working from a U.S. Bank location three (3) or more days per week.

If there’s anything we can do to accommodate a disability during any portion of the application or hiring process, please refer to our  disability accommodations for applicants .

Benefits:
Our approach to benefits and total rewards considers our team members’ whole selves and what may be needed to thrive in and outside work. That's why our benefits are designed to help you and your family boost your health, protect your financial security and give you peace of mind. Our benefits include the following:
- Healthcare (medical, dental, vision)

- Basic term and optional term life insurance

- Short-term and long-term disability

- Pregnancy disability and parental leave

- 401(k) and employer-funded retirement plan

- Paid vacation (from two to five weeks depending on salary grade and tenure)

- Up to 11 paid holiday opportunities

- Adoption assistance

- Sick and Safe Leave accruals of one hour for every 30 worked, up to 80 hours per calendar year unless otherwise provided by law

Review our full benefits available by employment status here .

U.S. Bank is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, religion, color, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or veteran status, and other factors protected under applicable law.

E-Verify
U.S. Bank participates in the U.S. Department of Homeland Security E-Verify program in all facilities located in the United States and certain U.S. territories. The E-Verify program is an Internet-based employment eligibility verification system operated by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. Learn more about the  E-Verify program .

The salary range reflects figures based on the primary location, which is listed first. The actual range for the role may differ based on the location of the role. In addition to salary, U.S. Bank offers a comprehensive benefits package, including incentive and recognition programs, equity stock purchase 401(k) contribution and pension (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). Pay Range: $117,000.00 - $150,000.00

U.S. Bank will consider qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records for employment. U.S. Bank conducts background checks consistent with applicable local laws, including the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance and the California Fair Chance Act as well as the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. U.S. Bank is subject to, and conducts background checks consistent with the requirements of Section 19 of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act (FDIA). In addition, certain positions may also be subject to the requirements of FINRA, NMLS registration, Reg Z, Reg G, OFAC, the NFA, the FCPA, the Bank Secrecy Act, the SAFE Act, and/or federal guidelines applicable to an agreement, such as those related to ethics, safety, or operational procedures.

Applicants must be able to comply with U.S. Bank policies and procedures including the Code of Ethics and Business Conduct and related workplace conduct and safety policies.

Posting may be closed earlier due to high volume of applicants.

jobs.title: Small Business Relationship Banker 1-2  -  Louisville, KY
jobs.description:
At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions and enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed.  We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive at every stage of your career. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.

Job Description
Responsible for demonstrating excellent customer service in accordance with the U.S. Bank Core Values while serving as the primary Small Business Banking partner for assigned branches and relationships and providing comprehensive financial solutions to small businesses with annual revenues between $500K and $2.5 million. Typically supporting two to three branch locations, the Small Business Relationship Banker acts as a dedicated resource for branch teams, helping to address complex small business client needs and opportunities. The Small Business Relationship Banker builds and deepens client relationships through proactive outreach, structured discovery, consultative selling, and disciplined follow-through. The role translates financial information, cash-flow dynamics, client goals, operating cycle considerations, and risk indicators into practical guidance and solution recommendations.

This job requires outside prospecting and sales activities to grow revenue and achieve assigned financial targets and growth goals. The banker identifies stated and unstated client priorities, aligns products and services to growth, efficiency, and risk objectives, and clearly articulates value, trade-offs, and next steps. Solutions may include business deposit products, lending and credit products, treasury management, payment solutions, business credit cards, digital tools, cash-flow tools, and other appropriate small-business solutions.

The role actively develops internal and external relationships, collaborates with branch partners, centers of influence, clients, and other business line partners, and maintains relationship ownership and coordination through handoff, decision, follow-up, activation, usage, and demonstrated client value. Through regular engagement with assigned branches, the banker shares referral outcomes, successful sales and service practices, and insights on newly established small business relationships to strengthen partnership effectiveness and client growth opportunities. The banker balances acquisition, deepening, and service while maintaining strong CRM discipline and responsible banking practices.

This role has multiple levels, open to candidates with 3 years minimum experience in customer service, consultative sales, networking, prospecting, and/or small-business banking . The successful candidate will be hired for the level of the position that aligns with their experience. Please note that the salary range provided corresponds to the lowest level of the position posted.

We are hiring for several roles: one role will support the Shively and Silver & Spring (IN) offices; one role will support the McMahan Plaza, Bashford Manor Kroger, and Highlands offices; the Bilingual Small Business Relationship Banker will support the Outer Loop Kroger and Audubon Park offices.

Required Qualifications:
-Bachelor’s degree in business, Accounting, Finance, or equivalent experience and job-related experience
-Three or more years of customer service, consultative sales, networking, prospecting, and/or small-business banking experience
-National Mortgage Licensing Service registration under the terms of the S.A.F.E. Act of 2008 and Regulation Z and ongoing compliance with all legal or regulatory registration requirements, including maintaining a satisfactory criminal and credit record
- Bilingual ability to read, write, and speak in business-level proficiency of Spanish and English required for the role supporting the Outer Loop Kroger and Audubon Park offices.

Desired Qualifications:
-Demonstrates excellent customer service in accordance with the U.S. Bank Core Values and provides comprehensive financial solutions to small businesses with annual revenues between $500K and $2.5 million
-Demonstrates strong written and verbal communication skills and can convey business recommendations in an effective manner
-Understands banking operations, product knowledge, sales, new business development, customer service and relationship management, community relations, pipeline management, and responsible banking practices

Location Expectations
This role requires working from a U.S. Bank location five (5) days per week.   This position also requires two or more hours of driving per week.

Compensation:
Total compensation includes base compensation in addition to eligibility for incentives based on the employee’s production under the applicable incentive plan.

jobs.description:
At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions, enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed in the right ways, all more confidently and more often—that’s what we call the courage to thrive.   We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.

As a wholly owned subsidiary of U.S. Bank, Elavon is committed to building the platforms and ecosystems that help over 1.5 million customers around the world to achieve their financial goals—no matter what they need. From transaction processing to customer service, to driving innovation and launching new products, we’re building a range of tailored payment solutions powered by the latest technology. As part of our team, you can explore what motivates and energizes your career goals: partnering with our customers, our communities, and each other.

We actively uphold transparent and fair hiring practices that support individual opportunity, inclusive culture, and career mobility across all levels of our organisation.

We offer meaningful opportunities for growth, a culture of inclusion, and a strong commitment to transparency and integrity in everything we do.

Job Description
The Senior Credit Analyst is a member of the 2nd Line of Defence Credit Risk Management function, reporting to the Head of Credit Portfolio Risk. The role centres on strategic duties, combining credit governance expertise and support to credit‑risk decisioning processes as well as focalized MI & Reporting responsibilities.
This role supports integration across the Credit Portfolio Risk workstreams through the oversight of credit governance structures, support of credit analysis and financial due diligence processes, and the provision of consistent, high‑quality, risk‑aligned management information to support informed decision‑making.

Key Responsibilities:

Credit Analysis and Financial Due Diligence
Support credit approvers through detailed credit analysis and financial due diligence, helping to inform sound credit decisions in line with established risk appetite, underwriting standards, concentration limits, and regulatory requirements.
Review underwriting proposals, annual reviews, renewals, amendments, waivers, and other credit requests to assess alignment with credit policy, risk appetite, approval conditions, and portfolio strategy.
Contribute to strong decision-making practices by participating in calibration sessions and monitoring approval trends under the guidance of senior management.
Credit Risk Governance
Support the effective operation of USBE Credit Risk governance bodies through end-to-end coordination of the Credit Committee and related working groups. The role holder will manage the administrative and governance activities required for these forums, including compiling and quality-checking materials from multiple stakeholders, coordinating meeting agendas and schedules, maintaining action logs and records, and ensuring papers are complete, accurate, and circulated on a timely basis.
This role will also support the Head of Credit Portfolio Risk to monitor adherence to the terms of reference and governance requirements for each forum, escalating issues where needed, and helping to ensure the overall efficiency, consistency, and proper functioning of these bodies.
Strategy & Portfolio Steering
Support the development and refinement of the bank’s credit portfolio strategy and risk appetite, ensuring alignment with evolving macroeconomic, regulatory, sectoral, and geopolitical trends.
This position serves as a subject matter expert, facilitating communication and alignment between strategic MI, governance structures, and the credit decision-making process.
Cross ‑ Functional Collaboration
Collaborate with Credit Risk team members and colleagues from other departments to uphold consistency and strong governance across credit-related reports, strategies, provisioning, and risk frameworks.

Preferred Skills/Experience:
- Bachelor’s degree in finance, Economics, Business, or a related field.

- Experience (4+ years) in credit risk, credit underwriting, portfolio risk, or credit approval support within a bank, regulated financial institution, credit fund, asset manager, insurer, or comparable financial services environment.

- Experience preparing or reviewing credit memos, underwriting proposals, annual reviews, risk rating assessments, covenant analysis, and committee materials.

- Effective written, presentation, and communication skills with the ability to articulate key messages in a concise manner.

- Analytical and problem-solving skills to interpret data/trends and draw actionable insights.

- Sound understanding of credit risk, methodologies, and regulatory requirements (e.g. Basel, CRR, EBA).

- Familiarity with financial analysis.

- Professional certifications such as FRM, CFA, ACA/ACCA or similar are desirable.

Additional information:
- The role offers a hybrid / flexible schedule, which means there's an in-office expectation of 3 or more days per week and the flexibility to work outside the office location for the other days.

This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

Total Rewards

We regularly review our compensation and benefits to ensure they remain competitive, inclusive, and responsive to employee needs and market trends. Further details of the compensation package will be provided upon application.

Job Description
Accelerate your career with us

The Funding & Securities Operations Analyst plays a critical role in supporting the operational execution, settlement oversight, and risk management of fixed income securities, debt issuance activities, and funding transactions. This position is responsible for end-to-end settlement support, fail management, TMPG compliance, new issue funding operations, underwriting support, and operational risk oversight across brokered CDs, bank notes, Treasury securities, and other fixed income products.

The successful candidate will partner closely with Treasury, Funding, Capital Markets, Trading, Middle Office, Finance, Risk, Technology, Operations teams, and external counterparties to ensure transactions settle accurately, funding obligations are met, regulatory requirements are satisfied, and operational risks are proactively mitigated.

Key Responsibilities
Securities Settlement, Fail Management & TMPG Oversight
- Monitor daily settlement activity and identify failed or at-risk securities transactions across fixed income and government securities products.
- Lead investigation, escalation, and resolution of settlement fails and operational exceptions.
- Monitor aged fails and implement escalation protocols based on financial, operational, counterparty, and regulatory impact.
- Engage with counterparties, custodians, clearing organizations, and internal partners to resolve settlement issues.
- Support compliance with Treasury Market Practices Group (TMPG) requirements, including fail charge monitoring, validation, reconciliation, and dispute resolution.
- Review fail trends, settlement performance, and exception activity to identify opportunities for risk reduction and process enhancement.
- Maintain documentation supporting fail investigations, settlements, TMPG activity, and control evidence.

Funding & New Issue Operations
- Manage the operational lifecycle of brokered certificates of deposit (CDs), bank notes, and other debt issuance transactions.
- Coordinate underwriting and funding activities across Treasury, Finance, Capital Markets, Legal, Operations, and external issuing agents.
- Review transaction documentation and settlement requirements to ensure operational readiness and timely execution.
- Monitor issuance pipelines and funding calendars to support successful transaction settlement.
- Support onboarding of new funding programs, structures, products, and issuance capabilities.
- Ensure funding transactions are executed within established deadlines and operational requirements.

Settlement & Wire Controls
- Review and validate wire instructions, settlement details, payment routing information, and beneficiary data.
- Establish and maintain settlement instructions, approved templates, and payment controls.
- Coordinate with Treasury, correspondent banks, trustees, custodians, and external agents to ensure accurate and timely delivery of funding proceeds.
- Investigate and resolve wire exceptions, rejected payments, settlement discrepancies, and funding delays.
- Maintain documentation supporting approvals, validations, settlements, and payment processing activities.

Risk Management & Controls
- Maintain a strong control framework supporting settlement activity, funding operations, and debt issuance processes.
- Escalate material settlement, funding, liquidity, operational, or reputational risks to leadership and key stakeholders.
- Support audits, compliance reviews, regulatory examinations, and risk management inquiries.
- Ensure adherence to internal policies, procedures, and control standards.
- Develop and maintain process documentation, desktop procedures, escalation protocols, and control evidence.

Analytics, Reporting & Process Improvement
- Develop and maintain reporting related to settlement performance, fail activity, funding transactions, underwriting operations, and operational exceptions.
- Analyze trends across fails, funding delays, wire rejections, operational breaks, and settlement exceptions.
- Perform root-cause analysis to identify recurring issues and opportunities for remediation.
- Track operational performance metrics and remediation efforts to measure improvements and reduce risk.
- Partner with Technology and Operations teams to implement automation, process simplification, and enhanced controls.

Business Partnership & Stakeholder Support
- Serve as a key operational contact for Funding, Treasury, Trading, Capital Markets, Finance, Risk, Technology, and external counterparties.
- Provide transparency on significant settlement and funding issues, including financial and operational impacts.
- Participate in governance discussions related to settlement effectiveness, funding operations, operational risk, and control enhancement.
- Support new product initiatives, business changes, and operational readiness assessments.
- Collaborate across teams to improve client, counterparty, and business partner experience while strengthening operational performance.

Underwrite new originations and portfolio exposures for a broad range of CRE asset classes.

Execute straightforward credit requests for existing clients with limited supervision

Support both existing property transactions (including refinancings) and ground‑up construction projects, including budget monitoring and monthly construction draw reviews through project completion

Proactively identify and communicate emerging risks, mitigants, and other issues at the transaction and portfolio level

Collaboration & Communication
Collaborate effectively with Credit Approvers and internal risk partners
Participate in client bank meetings, as needed, to support underwriting, portfolio management, and risk discussions
Serve as a reliable first line of credit analysis, escalating issues appropriately

Bachelor's degree, or equivalent work experience
Two or more years of experience in a finance/analytical related role

Strong foundation in CRE underwriting across multiple property types (cash flow, valuation, sponsor analysis, structure, and covenants).
Experience authoring credit memoranda and presenting key risks, mitigants, and recommendations to approval committees

Comfort operating with accountability—independently driving analyses while partnering closely with Relationship Managers, Portfolio Managers, and Credit Approvers
Familiarity with banking credit policy, loan documentation concepts, and CRE underwriting processes (construction, bridge, term, and portfolio facilities)
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel (cash flow modeling and scenario analysis) and the broader Microsoft Office Suite
Experience with nCino, CoStar, and/or other CRE research platforms preferred

Job Description
The Community Reinvestment Act (CRA) Self-Evaluation & Program Governance Analyst is responsible for developing an annual, cohesive, self-evaluation document by integrating data, analysis, and stakeholder input across the organization. This role combines data analysis, narrative development, and cross functional coordination to ensure the final product is accurate, consistent, well supported, and aligned with regulatory expectations. The annual CRA self-evaluation is the primary deliverable for this role, with additional responsibility for facilitating timely, coordinated responses and collaboration among business partners in support of related governance, audit, and regulatory examination activities.

Key Responsibilities

CRA Self-Evaluation
Data & Information Integration
- Gather and consolidate performance data, contextual information, and supporting documentation from cross functional partners; confirm source ownership, applicable reporting periods, and maintain appropriate source documentation and version control to support traceability.

Data Analysis, Interpretation & Narrative Development
- Analyze and interpret performance context, metrics, data tables, automated outputs, and peer or other comparative analyses to identify trends, gaps, inconsistencies, and meaningful insights that support the CRA self-evaluation.
- Draft, review, and / or refine clear, concise, and regulatory ready ratings support, summary narratives, performance explanations, and related regulatory examination materials.
- Create and maintain reusable narrative frameworks and standardized language, tone, structure, and terminology to support efficient, consistent, and scalable reporting.

CRA Self-Evaluation Assembly & Quality Assurance
- Compile and manage the full self-evaluation document, including tables and appendices.
- Perform quality assurance across self-evaluation data, narrative, and examination related deliverables to confirm that quantitative results are accurate, clearly explained, aligned with narrative conclusions, and consistent with other materials provided to the regulatory agency.
- Coordinate with data partners and other stakeholders to investigate and resolve discrepancies and finalize content.

CRA Program Governance
- Coordinate with the CRA Program Office and business partners to support governance routines, audit requests, regulatory examination responses, and related procedure and documentation needs.
- Track deliverables and open items, coordinate inputs and reviews, and assess supporting materials for accuracy, completeness, and timely completion.
- Assist with other CRA Program reporting needs and issue management administration in Archer, including maintaining records and supporting issue tracking and follow-up as needed.

Basic Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.
- Typically more than eight years of applicable experience

Preferred Qualifications

- Strong analytical and judgment skills, with the ability to interpret complex datasets and tables, challenge assumptions, identify emerging risks, and escalate material issues.

- Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to producing accurate, high-quality deliverables.
- Strong written communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex information into clear, structured materials for compliance, governance, audit, or regulatory audiences.

- Strong project management and prioritization skills, with the ability to manage multiple stakeholders and deadlines for an annual enterprise wide deliverable in a collaborative environment.
- Experience in the Community Reinvestment Act, fair lending, compliance program management, compliance risk management, or related regulatory compliance functions, including support for regulatory examinations and internal audit requests.
- Experience supporting governance routines and developing, maintaining, or reviewing compliance and regulatory documentation.

- Familiarity with CRA rating methodologies and performance context development.

- Proficiency with Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Archer, and data driven reporting or visualization tools, including experience working with templates and automated outputs.

jobs.title: Senior Credit Analyst
jobs.description:
At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions and enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed.  We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive at every stage of your career. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.

Job Description
The Senior Credit Analyst is part of Institutional Risk Management within Credit Risk Management and serves as a second line of defense. The senior analyst researches and analyzes financial institution, clearing house entities, GSE and sovereign (country) credit fundamentals based on underwriting standards, assigns ratings within the context of credit policy, and recommends credits for approval. Financial institutions include foreign banks, and broker dealers. The senior analyst evaluates the financial institution’s operating environment, management, ownership, market position/concentration, financial performance, strengths/weaknesses, and trends in the context of the economic and political environment of the bank's domicile country (sovereign risk). The senior analyst establishes limits and conducts annual reviews for various counterparty activities for individual financial institutions and countries. Business lines supported include International Financial Institutions, Correspondent Banking, Foreign Exchange, Corporate Treasury, Capital Markets, Corporate Payment Systems, Mortgage, Leasing, Wealth Management, Trust, and others. The position regularly evolves to include credit approval responsibilities.

Partners with their assigned Line of Business, other Risk/Compliance/Audit (RCA) professionals, and RCA Managers to, depending on their function, create, implement, maintain, review or oversee an effective risk management framework. Participates in projects and/or activities that ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations. Identifies gaps and inform solutions that minimize losses resulting from inadequate internal processes, systems or human errors. Identifies, responds and/or escalates risks as appropriate. Serves as a functional liaison between the Line of Business and the Lines of Defense.

Key Responsibilities:
- Research and analyze the creditworthiness of financial institutions, foreign banks, broker-dealers, clearing organizations, government-sponsored entities, and sovereigns.

- Perform due diligence and complete credit underwriting in accordance with established underwriting standards and credit policy.

- Assess operating environment, management, ownership, market position, concentrations, financial performance, key strengths and weaknesses, and relevant trends.

- Analyze sovereign and country risk, including the economic and political environment affecting counterparties.

- Assign internal credit ratings and probability-of-default assessments and prepare well-supported recommendations for approval.

- Establish, review, and manage credit limits for financial institutions, countries, and related counterparty activities.
- Collaborate with Line of Business partners, Risk, Compliance, Audit, and other lines of defense to support an effective risk management framework

Basic Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree, or equivalent work experience
- Typically more than six years of applicable experience

Preferred Skills/Experience
- Two to three years of counterparty credit underwriting experience, preferably within a larger financial institution managing complex institutional exposures.
- Experience analyzing financial institutions, foreign banks, sovereign or country risk, broker-dealers, clearing organizations, or government-sponsored entities
- Commercial credit underwriting experience may be considered when direct counterparty underwriting experience is not available.
- Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, including the ability to evaluate complex information, market conditions, and global economic or political developments.
- Strong interpersonal, relationship-management, collaboration, and influencing skills across multiple business lines and stakeholder groups.
- Intellectual curiosity and an interest in global markets, economic developments, foreign banking systems, and country risk.

Job Description
Job Description
- PCS is seeking a Manager to lead Bankruptcy, Offensive Litigation, and Debt Settlement Company (DSC) Servicing team(s) who may be responsible for coding of new bankruptcy notifications and updates, filing bankruptcy proof of claims, qualifying accounts for offensive litigation actions and partnering with Law Firms to ensure accuracy of legal documents, and researching legal matters, as well as any additional activities that may occur through the lifecycle of bankruptcy, litigation actions and resolving accounts with DSC’s.  Incumbent leads the day-to-day
- Operations and ensure team members facilitate processes, etc., to ensure compliance with policy and procedures.
The ideal candidate will understand Collections & Recovery, and/or Bankruptcy Operations.
- Additionally, this person will have proven leadership skills in coaching, developing, and holding team members accountable to performance standards.  They will ensure compliance with applicable internal policies and procedures, regulatory requirements, and federal bankruptcy law.
- Ensures compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations and policies and internal operating policies, procedures, and audit/examining standards.  Responds to audit/examining exceptions.
- Monitors tracking and performance.
- Provides required reporting to keep executive management appraised of activities; makes presentations as needed.
- Communicate with leaders and staff to produce effective procedures and workflow and to ensure quality service levels are maintained. Follows up with resolution of problems to ensure timely response and customer satisfaction.
Recommends hires, transfers, terminations, salary adjustments, performance standards and reviews.  May approve employee daily time records, work assignments, vacations, sick pay, etc.  Executes employee relations, training and affirmative action policies as needed.
- Creates and develops ongoing performance reviews and administers performance improvement plans if needed.
- Directly and through staff, manages and coordinates the operational activities for assigned functional area(s)/region(s).  Ensure quality service and effective operations support for all assigned internal and external customers.  Leads high-performance teams of both entry level and skilled professionals by setting goals, providing ongoing feedback, measuring progress while recognizing success and building accountability with employees.
- Oversee adherence to corporate policies and procedures and ensures compliance with applicable laws and regulations within area of responsibility.  Participates in the review and improvement of operational systems and procedures relevant to assigned units.

Role Responsibilities
- Lead the day-to-day operations of Bankruptcy, Offensive Litigation, and Debt Settlement Company servicing teams.
- Oversee the coding and maintenance of new bankruptcy notifications, case updates, and related account records.
Ensure accurate and timely preparation and filing of bankruptcy proofs of claim.
- Direct the review and qualification of accounts for offensive litigation in accordance with approved criteria.
- Partner with external law firms to validate legal documents, resolve discrepancies, and support timely litigation activity.
- Oversee legal and account research throughout the bankruptcy, litigation, and debt settlement lifecycles.
- Manage account resolution activities involving Debt Settlement Companies and other authorized third parties.
- Ensure compliance with internal policies, operating procedures, regulatory requirements, and federal bankruptcy law.
- Respond to audit and examination findings, implement corrective actions, and maintain audit-ready controls and documentation.
- Monitor team productivity, quality, service levels, and operational performance against established standards.
- Prepare management reporting, communicate trends and risks, and deliver presentations to executive leadership as needed.
- Develop and improve procedures and workflows in partnership with leaders and staff to strengthen efficiency and service quality.
- Resolve operational issues and escalations promptly to support customer satisfaction and appropriate account outcomes.
- Coach, develop, and hold employees accountable through regular feedback, performance reviews, and performance improvement plans.
Support staffing and employee administration, including hiring recommendations, work assignments, time records, leave requests, compensation actions, training, employee relations, and applicable employment policies.

Competencies:
- People Leadership & Team Management
- Coaching, Development & Performance Management
- Collections and Recovery Operations
- Bankruptcy Servicing & Federal Bankruptcy Law
- Offensive Litigation Management
- Debt Settlement Company Servicing
- Regulatory Compliance & Risk Management
- Policy and Procedure Administration
- Audit and Examination Response
- Operational Performance Monitoring
- Reporting & Executive Presentations
- Workflow and Process Improvement
- Legal Document Accuracy & Research
- Law Firm and Stakeholder Management
- Problem Resolution & Decision-Making
- Customer Service & Quality Assurance
- Workforce Planning & Employee Relations
- Accountability and Results Orientation
- Written and Verbal Communication

Skills:
- Leadership and Team Management
- Collections and Recovery Operations
- Bankruptcy Operations and Servicing
- Regulatory Compliance and Risk Management
- Employee Coaching and Development
- Performance Management and Accountability
- Legal Research and Document Review
- Operational Performance Monitoring and Reporting
- Process and Workflow Improvement

Stakeholder, Law Firm, and Executive Communication

Qualifications:

Basic Qualifications  - Bachelor’s degree, or equivalent work experience  - Typically three or more years of relevant experience  Preferred Skills/Experience  - Thorough knowledge of operational functions, systems, procedures, various products and/or services supported by the assigned area(s) - Understanding of applicable Federal and State laws and regulations - Thorough knowledge of applicable products, programs, financial analysis and related documentation as applicable - Good organizational, managerial and project management skills - Well-developed customer relations skills - Excellent interpersonal and verbal and written communication skills - Excellent supervisory and management skills - Ability to manage multiple tasks.

Years of experience : 8+ relevant years.
Leadership experience : 3+ years.
Shift Timings: 6:30pm-3:30 AM IST

jobs.title: Business Banking Senior Relationship Manager- South Bay/Long Beach - Potential Signing Bonus up to $25K
jobs.description:
At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions and enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed.  We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive at every stage of your career. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.

Job Description
Our Business Banking Relationship Managers combine sales expertise, relationship management, and financial acumen to help business clients achieve their goals.

By developing new client relationships, deepening existing partnerships, and delivering tailored financial solutions, you'll play a key role in helping businesses thrive while growing your own career.
In this role, you'll serve as a trusted advisor to business owners, connecting them with lending, treasury management, deposit, and payment solutions that support every stage of growth.

Backed by a team of specialists and a full suite of industry-leading products, you'll have the resources and support to deliver meaningful results for your clients and your portfolio.

If you're energized by building relationships, driving business growth, and making a real impact in your community, we'd love to connect with you!

**U.S. Bank offers a robust, market‑leading Business Banking compensation plan that rewards the full scope of your relationship‑building efforts—from loan generation to deposit growth to fee‑based production.
If you're ready to elevate your career and maximize your earning potential, apply today to learn more about the plan and explore the exciting opportunities available!

**This role may offer a sign on bonus up to $25,000 depending on qualifications and business considerations
Role responsibilities include:
- Allocate 65–70% of time to active prospecting, self‑sourcing business, building a book from the ground up, and driving new client acquisition.

- Build, develop, enrich and manage new and existing relationships with business clients.

- Deliver financial expertise and client-centric solutions that build strong, long-term relationships.

- Assess and attend to clients' banking needs.

- Educate clients on available deposit and loan products and services.

- Recommend financial solutions based on each client’s unique goals and needs.

- Partner effectively with Treasury Management, Merchant Services and Business Banking Credit Card teams.

Basic Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree, or equivalent work experience
- Seven or more years of relevant experience

Preferred Skills/Experience
- Knowledge of local market
-Strong business‑to‑business sales skills, with the ability to independently source and grow a book of business
- Strong business development acumen, grounded in effective sales practices and process discipline
- Strong interpersonal and collaboration skills, with the ability to partner across multiple business lines
- Proven track record onboarding and retaining businesses with annual revenues between $2.5MM and $50MM
-Consistent track record of meeting measurable performance goals across quantitative and qualitative metrics

Location
If not meeting with clients, this role requires working from a U.S. Bank location three (3) or more days per week.

If there’s anything we can do to accommodate a disability during any portion of the application or hiring process, please refer to our  disability accommodations for applicants .
